To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the formation of the out-of-sequence Lewis thrust system was a long-term process and that it involved the development of a complex series of duplex structures that were not all formed at the same time.
the Lewis thrust is a composite surface that is the product of several generations of thrust faulting.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) determining the structural and stratigraphic relationships among the structures within the hanging wall of the Lewis thrust, (2) determining the relative ages of the structures within the duplex and the Lewis II thrust, (3) determining the relative timing of the formation of the duplex and Lewis II thrust with respect to one another, (4) determining the relative age of the duplex and the formation of the Lewis II thrust with the Lewis thrust, and (5) determining the relative time of
the structural evolution of the Spot Mountain duplex and the Lewis thrust system in the Lewis overthrust belt of southeastern Montana and northeastern Wyoming.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Lewis thrust is a composite surface that formed out of sequence in the southeastern part of Glacier National Park.
the Lewis thrust was active at some time during or after the formation of the Spot Mountain duplex.
the Lewis II thrust is a composite thrust surface composed of multiple thrusts that were active over an extended period of time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Lewis thrust system was formed by out-of-sequence faulting and duplexing, and that these structures are the product of the same tectonic processes that produced the Lewis thrust system.
the Lewis thrust system is not the simple, planar, and continuous structure that has been previously assumed.
we have documented the formation of a duplex within the hanging wall of the Lewis thrust.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Spot Mountain duplex is not the product of simple duplex growth, but rather the result of multiple episodes of thrusting and duplex formation that have been reworked by subsequent out-of-sequence displacement.
the Spot Mountain duplex formed in a structurally higher position than its present-day location, and that the duplex is now truncated by the Lewis thrust.
the formation of duplexes in the hanging wall of the Lewis thrust is not a necessary consequence of the out-of-sequence formation of the Lewis thrust.
